latest_release.body:
# CrossWatch v0.14.7

**Release:**
v0.14.7 improves database cleanup and makes Events faster and easier to follow. Tools brings the utilities together and Backup & Restore gets its own page.
Some old Trakt fallback code is gone too. Yes, even CW once used Trakt as the default.

**Upgrade notes:**
Sync pair state migrates automatically without starting over. Old event and pair data is cleaned up in the background. 
The notification bell suggests Optimize database when space can be reclaimed.
Opening scrobble history for the first time may take longer while its activity index is built.

## ✨ Highlights
- **Improved Events:** Grouped actions, provider icons, destination results, bulk review and easier navigation.
- **Smaller databases:** Daily cleanup removes leftover pair state and trims repeated failures while preserving run results.
- **Captures and backups:** Both have Events tabs, with failed and scheduled runs also shown in Hub activity.
- **Tools menu:** Events, Logs, Editor, Analyzer, Import and the new Backup & Restore page together, including mobile navigation.
- **Unknown watch dates:** sync between Trakt, WeTrakr, SIMKL and CW Tracker. 

## 🔧 Fixes & Improvements
- **Improved:** Faster Events loading and pagination for large archives.
- **Improved:** Cleanup waits for active syncs and maintenance.
- **Improved:** better scheduler status.
- **Improved:** Fanart 4K background support and show artwork fallback when episode stills are missing.
- **Fixed:** Episode artwork and metadata lookups using episode IDs instead of show IDs.
- **Fixed:** Missing parent-show IDs in Plex webhook and watcher ratings.
- **Fixed:** Activity status, timestamps, progress, destination timelines and filter resets.
- **Fixed:** Unsupported Plex episode ratings now appear as skipped with a reason.
- **Fixed:** Plex webhook lookups respect SSL verification settings.
- **Fixed:** Plex library skips, including shows split across libraries.
- **Fixed:** Ratings and scrobbles use the selected account and report the correct destination.
- **Fixed:** PunchPlay and Scrob webhook scrobbles work again; failures appear for every target.
- **Fixed:** Token refreshes no longer reset or duplicate sync pair state.
- **Fixed:** Backup and restore actions stay locked until complete or restarting.
- **Fixed:** Stuck running syncs in Events and Loading chips in Hub Progress.
- **Fixed:** Copy buttons on macOS and HTTP, with selectable webhook URLs.
- **Fixed:** Last successful sync and readable profile names.
- **Updated:** WeTrakr adapter to `v1.0`.
- **Updated:** CrossWatch to `v0.14.7`.

detail.readme:
# CrossWatch **CrossWatch (CW)** tracks what you watch through Watcher and syncs your watchlists, ratings, history, playback progress and collections across supported media servers and trackers. **Watcher doesn't need Plex Pass or Emby Premiere.** Set up multiple Watcher routes for your servers and users, and sync pairs between media servers, between trackers, or from a server to a tracker. CW runs locally, with a web UI and a CLI to manage it all.

⭐ Star this repository to get updates


## Why CW? **Watcher doesn't need Plex Pass or Emby Premiere.** Set up multiple routes for your servers and users, and send playback activity to their chosen supported destinations. You can also keep media servers in sync with each other, connect them to trackers, or sync between trackers. Choose what each pair syncs: watch history, playback progress, watchlists, ratings or collections, depending on provider support. Run pairs manually or on a schedule. Manage it all from one place: accounts, Watcher routes, syncs, current playback and a combined watchlist. Profiles keep your setup separate from those of friends and family. Keep your data with you, without being tied to one tracker. Sync it across the services you use and keep local snapshots in the CW Tracker. When you need more control, Interactive Sync lets you review changes before applying them. The Analyzer helps you check missing items, and saved mappings let you fix wrong matches, anime episode numbering, and split or combined episodes for future syncs. ## Features - Watcher with multiple routes for different servers and users. **No Plex Pass or Emby Premiere needed.** - Server-to-server, server-to-tracker and tracker-to-tracker sync, where supported. - Watchlists, ratings, history, playback progress and collections. Rewatches too, for supported trackers. - Multiple accounts, separate profiles and managed users who can handle their own pairs, routes and schedule. - Interactive Sync to review additions, updates and removals before applying them. - Webhook scrobbling for supported providers. - Custom mappings for wrong matches, anime IDs, and split or combined episodes. - A local CW Tracker with snapshots of your server and tracker data. - Optional AI help: ask CrossWatch advice with your own AI model. It can suggest. You can also give AI apps like Claude, Codex or Cursor read-only access. Off until you set it up. ## Supported integrations CW works with Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Silo, Tofa, SIMKL, Floppy, FlickList, Trakt, WeTrakr, AniList, MyAnimeList (MAL), Kitsu, TMDb, MDBList, PublicMetaDB, PunchPlay, BingeBase, Scrob, Tautulli, Tracearr, Kodi, Nuvio, Stremio and its own local CW Tracker. Not every integration supports every feature. Some sync lists and history; others report playback activity. Setup details are in the [wiki](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/). ## Installation The examples below use Docker. See the [installation guide](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/getting-started/installation) for more details. ### Docker Compose Save this as `compose.yaml`: ```yaml services: crosswatch: image: ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest container_name: crosswatch ports: - "8787:8787" environment: TZ: Europe/Amsterdam volumes: - crosswatch_config:/config restart: unless-stopped volumes: crosswatch_config: ``` Change `TZ` to your timezone, then run this from the same folder: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` ### Docker run Or run it directly from Bash: ```bash docker run -d \ --name crosswatch \ -p 8787:8787 \ -v crosswatch_config:/config \ -e TZ=Europe/Amsterdam \ --restart unless-stopped \ ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest ``` Both examples store persistent data in a Docker volume mounted at `/config`. Keep that volume when replacing or updating the container. ### Your first sync Open [http://localhost:8787](http://localhost:8787). If Docker is running on another machine, use that machine's address with port `8787`. 1. Connect the accounts you want to use. 2. Create a sync pair: choose which services to connect and what to sync. 3. Run the pair and check the results. Use Interactive Sync if you'd like to review changes before applying them. 4. Add a schedule if you want it to run automatically. See the [first-time setup guide](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/getting-started/first-time-setup) for the full setup. ## Scrobbling **Watcher** reports playback from Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, Silo, Tofa, Kodi and Scrob to supported trackers. No Plex Pass or Emby Premiere needed for Watcher. You can also use **webhooks** from Plex, Emby and Jellyfin. Anime ID mapping is available for Watcher and webhooks with supported providers. ### Kodi The [CrossWatch for Kodi add-on](https://github.com/crosswatch-app/kodi-addon) reports playback and household viewers. It also supports ratings directly in the add-on. Set up a Watcher route per viewer and they each get their own history, even when sharing a Kodi profile. ## Mappings Sometimes the same episode has a different number on another service, or a title gets matched to the wrong movie. You can correct titles, IDs, seasons and episodes, then save the mapping for future syncs. Split and combined episodes are supported, and you can import or export your mappings. Anime ID mapping, powered by AniBridge and animeApi, supports AniList, MyAnimeList, Kitsu, SIMKL and CW Tracker pairs. ## Tools Use the **Analyzer** when something hasn't synced as expected. You can compare snapshots, find missing items and watch time differences, fix wrong matches, check pending retries and release blocked items. | Tool | What you can do | | --- | --- | | Editor | Inspect, add or block items, manage saved mappings, and handle split or combined episodes. | | Sync topology advisor | See your sync routes and spot overlapping paths. | | Playback Progress Manager | View and edit unfinished playback sessions across providers. | | Import and Export | Import tracker files or export your data. | | Events and Logs | Look through sync history, investigate problems, and filter logs by pair or run. | | Captures | Roll back provider watchlists, ratings and history. | There's also a unified watchlist, a player card showing what's playing, and notifications for sync progress and pending reviews. Schedules can be simple or configured per pair. For Plex, you can import history for removed items into your CW Tracker. ## Backup and recovery Use **Backup & Restore** to back up CrossWatch (including mappings, blocks and custom anime rules), selected CW trackers and saved captures. Save locally, with an optional copy to Nextcloud/WebDAV or a mounted folder. Schedule automatic backups, follow their progress and restore saved data from the same dialog. Recover one tracker as a new instance, or restore only mappings and blocks, custom anime rules or saved captures. Mount optional backup storage at `/backups`, or set `CW_BACKUP_ROOT` to another absolute path inside the container. ## Running without the web UI Add `-e CW_CLI_ONLY=1` to the Docker command, or `CW_CLI_ONLY: "1"` under `environment` in Compose. The API, CLI, webhooks and auth callbacks keep working. ## Run once and exit For cron, Kubernetes CronJobs or another external scheduler, use `run-once`. Set up your accounts and sync pairs first: ```bash docker run --rm \ -v crosswatch_config:/config \ -e TZ=Europe/Amsterdam \ ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest \ run-once ``` Use the volume that contains your existing configuration. If you set up CW with Compose, its volume name normally includes the Compose project name; replace `crosswatch_config` above with that volume's actual name. To run specific pairs, use their IDs, numbers or unique prefixes. Replace the example IDs below with your own: ```bash docker run --rm \ -v crosswatch_config:/config \ ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest \ run-once --pair pair_07c3 --pair pair_91ab ``` The command exits with `0` on success and `1` if the sync reports errors or cancellation. Add `--fail-on-unresolved` if you also want unmatched items to fail the job. ## Help and feedback Setup docs are in the [wiki](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/). For questions and discussion, there's [r/CrossWatchApp](https://www.reddit.com/r/CrossWatchApp/) and the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/c9cjzHGve). Please report bugs in [Issues](https://github.com/cenodude/CrossWatch/issues), with steps to reproduce them and what went wrong. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before sending a PR. For security reports, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). The license is in [LICENSE](LICENSE). ## Support and sponsors

Every cent donated through Buy Me a Coffee goes directly to the **ALS Foundation in the Netherlands**.

Thanks to our sponsors for supporting CW.
